solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rang boutique — ordered sachet for kitchen

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are put in a new order, as if ordered or arranged

explanation.surface: A shop owner rings a boutique and orders a herb sachet for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rang' and 'ordered' read as past-tense verbs of a phone order; 'ordered' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic French cooking aid: a small bundle or muslin bag of herbs used to flavour stews and stocks.

clue.text: Crime of dealer in stolen goods

parts.note: a fence is slang for a receiver of stolen property

explanation.surface: A police charge sheet: the crime committed by a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach of the law is a synonym for a crime or misdeed.

clue.text: As monarch, Veronica quite extraordinary

indicators.note: the words are made extra-ordinary, put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A woman called Veronica is remarkable in the role of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the British monarch who reigned from 1837 to 1901.

clue.text: Got out, thrilled to avoid the cold

indicators.note: the word for thrilled must avoid, that is drop, the cold letter

parts.note: thrilled means excited
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone left the building, delighted to escape the chilly weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Left or departed: a synonym for going out of a place.

clue.text: Prepare for ordeal: use abrasive dentifrice?

definitions.meaning: to steel yourself to endure something unpleasant
literally, to put grit on your teeth by brushing with a gritty toothpaste

explanation.surface: A grim choice of toothpaste as preparation for a trying day.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for summoning determination before facing something hard, read literally as scouring the teeth with grit.

clue.text: Fearsome beast makes Greek character keep at home

indicators.note: the Greek letter keeps, or holds, the word for at home within it

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R
in means at home

explanation.surface: A terrifying creature drives a Greek person to stay indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A large horned African or Asian animal, an example of a dangerous beast.

clue.text: One litre fewer, round middle of evening — it makes me sick

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the word for fewer goes round the next letter

parts.note: fewer means less

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter word evening

explanation.surface: A drinker cuts back by a litre in the evening, finding it otherwise makes them ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease or ailment is what causes one to feel unwell, so the clue speaks as the sickness.

clue.text: Hit, say, to cover

indicators.note: say tells us the word for hit is spoken, giving a word of the same pronunciation

parts.note: to hit sharply is to rap

explanation.surface: A fragment of a manual: strike, for instance, in order to cover something.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose something in paper or cloth is to cover it, a synonym.

clue.text: Cause annoyance, grabbing fine weapon

indicators.note: the word for annoying grabs, holding inside, the letter for fine

parts.note: to rile is to irritate
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a nuisance by snatching a perfectly good gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled gun fired from the shoulder, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: First to mark as read, perhaps

definitions.meaning: coming at the start, as the opening stage
to sign one's abbreviated name on a document to show it has been seen

explanation.surface: An office instruction: the first thing to do is mark the memo as read.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means at the beginning; as a verb it means to sign with one's letters, as on a circulated memo.

clue.text: Unknown having to leave Cornish town in expiation

indicators.note: the unknown letter has to leave, dropping out of the town's name

parts.note: Penzance is a town at the far west of Cornwall, in south-west England
Z is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An outsider is made to quit a Cornish town as atonement.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-punishment done to atone for wrongdoing is a near synonym of making amends.

clue.text: Gas round area

parts.note: O is round in shape
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Gas spreads around the whole district.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, an example of a gas.

clue.text: Good reputation: Conservative and Socialist have it

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the British party
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Political commentary: both the Tory and the Socialist enjoy standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing or esteem earned from others, as in a deed that does one credit.

clue.text: Artist's conversation cut short with bitterness

indicators.note: the word for conversation is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a chat is a conversation
gall is bitterness or rancour

explanation.surface: A painter's talk ends abruptly, soured by resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Artist reads as 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter of dreamlike scenes, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Responds in scripture lesson, given part of Bible

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, the school subject in Britain
Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A pupil answers in a religion class after being set a passage of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaves in answer to something: a synonym for replies or answers.

clue.text: In church, one thin South American

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
lean means thin

explanation.surface: A skinny South American sits alone in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Chile is one kind of South American.

clue.text: Happen to acquire pass

definitions.meaning: to obtain something, often by chance
to drop in or go past, as a visitor might

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to obtain and to visit briefly in passing.

clue.text: A university degree is targeted from the first examination

indicators.note: from the first tells us to take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A student's university degree is aimed at from the outset of an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of accounts is a kind of examination.

clue.text: Exterminator in valley beginning to kill

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A hitman in a valley starts to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daleks are the robotic villains of the BBC series Doctor Who, whose catchphrase is 'Exterminate!'.
explanation.definitionFit: These television creatures exist to wipe out all other life, hence their famous cry.

clue.text: In dock, going to make test voyage?

parts.note: a machine that is on is going or working
to trial a ship is to take it on a test voyage

explanation.surface: A ship in dock is about to go out for its sea trials.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant standing in the dock of a court is being tried for a crime.

clue.text: Old Testament character, hard and reluctant

parts.note: Lot is Abraham's nephew in Genesis
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A biblical figure who was tough and unwilling.
explanation.definitionFit: An older spelling meaning unwilling, a synonym.

clue.text: Not recaptured as a body

definitions.meaning: an escaped prisoner still free is said to be loose
taken as a whole, as in the public generally

explanation.surface: A news snippet about an escapee still free in society as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both still free after escaping and in general, as with society as a whole.

clue.text: Bale out from European plane, leaving a hundred inside

indicators.note: the hundred goes inside the word for plane

parts.note: a jet is a plane
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A pilot parachutes from a European aircraft, leaving a hundred passengers aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thrown clear of an aircraft by ejector seat is to bail out of it.

clue.text: Not be choosy very much

definitions.meaning: to be happy with whatever comes along, fond of every option
an informal intensifier, as in running fast and hard

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means to enjoy whatever is offered; as an idiom it means intensely or with great vigour.
